Subject: Private deployment - maintenance blackout, ops bridge & staged rollback plan

Team / CloudNova ops,

Following up from the architecture review last week — attaching a concise plan for the upcoming maintenance window on the Private fleet in us-west-2. This is a coordinated patch + minor version update that requires a brief blackout on the control-plane roll (we will not evict tenant traffic unless we hit the canary failure criteria). High-level asks:

- Confirm final blackout window (proposal below) and any customer blackout conflicts.
- Ops bridge leads (primary + backup).
- Finalize canary scope and the exact rollback triggers we will enforce.
- Sign off on the preflight checklist (attached) and a single dry-run 48h prior.

Proposed schedule (UTC):
- Canary slice: 2026-11-17 02:00 - 02:30 UTC (5% of capacity)
- Full blackout (control-plane patch): 2026-11-17 03:00 - 04:30 UTC (planned drain + apply)
- Warm-up and verification: 2026-11-17 04:30 - 05:30 UTC

Rollback triggers (draft):
1) Canary error-rate > 3% sustained for 10m AND token latency P50 increase > 60ms vs baseline.
2) Any KV cache corruption detected on canary nodes.
3) Unexpected control-plane restarts > 2 in 10m.

If a rollback is required we will:
- Halt further slices, mark the release as shelved, and run the quick-evacuation lane to unpin to previous version.
- Run the compact rollback play (attached) to restore KV snapshots and rollback kernels.

Attachments: blackout-window-plan.pdf (timeline + stakeholders), preflight-checklist.csv, rollback-play-compact.md

Please reply with your confirmations / objections by EOD PT today so I can lock the Doc and send invites.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Product Ops, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private deployment - maintenance blackout, ops bridge & staged rollback plan

Thanks Vanessa — quick technical clarifications and a suggested compact rollback sequence:

1) Canary scope: include only control-plane + routing proxies (no stateful KV hosts). If canary passes, we expand to 20% and then full. This minimizes risk to runtime state.

2) Drain behavior: use soft-drain for 5m, then hard-evict if connections exceed N=50 open streams on a node after soft window.

3) Rollback (compact):
   - Step 1: mark release as "shelved" in orchestration and disable new scheduling to patched kernel.
   - Step 2: trigger KV snapshot restore from t-10m (we keep rolling snapshots on private by default).
   - Step 3: revert container image tag + restart proxies with graceful backfill.
   - Step 4: sanity checks: health-checks x10 (30s cadence) and end-to-end synthetic request suite.

I attached a trimmed preflight CSV and a compact rollback note. I also added an exact metric query for the latency/rate triggers (see row 7 in checklist).

Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
